prompt: An empty delivery van weighs $3{,}200$ pounds. It is loaded with boxes weighing $45$ pounds each, and it must cross a bridge with a weight limit of $5{,}000$ pounds. What is the maximum number of boxes the van can carry across the bridge?
hint: Total weight is the van plus the boxes, and it must stay at or below the limit.

hints.text: Total weight is the van plus the boxes, and it must stay at or below the limit.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller numbers: a $10$-pound cart with a $25$-pound limit, carrying $5$-pound boxes. That leaves $15$ pounds, so $3$ boxes. Subtract the fixed weight, then divide by the per-item weight.

learningObjective: Solve a real-world capacity inequality with a whole-number answer.
explanation: The loaded weight is $3200 + 45b$, and it must satisfy $3200 + 45b \le 5000$.
Divide: $b \le 40$. Since $1800 \div 45 = 40$ exactly, the van can carry $40$ boxes and hit the limit precisely.

alternativeExplanations.title: When to round down, and when not to
steps: If the division had come out to $40.7$, the answer would be $40$ — you cannot load a fraction of a box.
Here it divides evenly, and "$\le$" permits equality, so $40$ is achievable rather than one too many.
The rule: for a maximum with $\le$, take the floor of the quotient; an exact quotient is itself the answer.
